source_review: Only direct_wasm_scan.h differs from the shipped36-header baseline. Upstream revision and both patches match; current and frozen final source/compiler identities agree.

Exact scalar pattern remains unchanged: stable private plain-i64 cursor/count/last, byte equality literal, stride1/2/4/8, fixed storage or private packed slice. Debug, owners, effectful bodies, captures, addressed locals, accumulator aliases and possible prefix mappings reject.

Whole logical and widened physical span guards prove every loaded byte valid, including unselected stride lanes. Invalid or zero-trip cases retain the sole original scalar loop; no callback or new potentially trapping operation is introduced.
Two16-byte comparison bitmasks merge by unsigned high-mask shift16 and OR, then a uint32 lane mask. Bit31 is defined; all strides divide16 and32, preserving relative lane selection.
popcnt accumulation preserves nondebug modulo-i64 count. Last uses candidate/old-last/mask/select: clz(0) and discarded candidate arithmetic cannot trap; same-value private writes are unobservable.

After repeated32-byte groups the residual is below32, so at most one guarded16-byte vector pass suffices. Remaining scalar iterations preserve cursor overshoot, exact last index and trap order. The16-byte loop wrapper has no backedge.

No payload writes or callbacks occur, and all fast loads are proven nontrapping; delaying private accumulator updates until both loads complete is unobservable. No runtime ABI, memory layout or host behavior changes.
